title: AND-normalization preserves the literal count
statement: Let $c$ be a Boolean circuit on $n$ variables, and let $c'$ be the normal-form AND circuit obtained by normalizing it (a literal becomes a singleton clause, an AND gate normalizes each child to OR-normal form, and an OR gate is wrapped as a single OR node over the AND-normalizations of its children). Then $c'$ contains exactly as many literal occurrences as $c$: the number of literals in $c'$ equals the number of literals in $c$.
hypotheses_covered: c is a Boolean circuit on n variables (no additional constraint)
